questions.question: Which among the following vitamins influences iron absorption?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vitamin C**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vitamin C** influences iron absorption **by increasing the solubility of iron** in** the stomach and enhancing** its absorption in the small intestine.
 
• Vitamin C also helps in the conversion of ferric iron to ferrous iron, which is more easily absorbed by the body.
 
• Vitamin C-rich foods include citrus fruits, strawberries, kiwi, tomatoes, and bell peppers.
 
• Iron absorption may be reduced by consuming foods or supplements high in calcium, tannins, or phytates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

**Additional Information__**

 
• Iron is an essential mineral required for the production of hemoglobin, a protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen throughout the body.
 
• Iron deficiency can lead to anemia, fatigue, weakness, and impaired immune function.
 
• Good dietary sources of iron include red meat, poultry, fish, beans, lentils, spinach, and fortified cereals.
 
• Vitamin B: While B vitamins play a role in energy metabolism and red blood cell production, they do not directly influence iron absorption.
 
• Vitamin D: Vitamin D is important for calcium absorption and bone health, but it does not affect iron absorption.
 
• Vitamin K: Vitamin K is necessary for blood clotting and bone health, but it does not impact iron absorption.

questions.question: Which of the following are building blocks of proteins?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amino acids**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Amino acids** are organic compounds that serve as the building blocks of proteins in living organisms.
 
• Proteins are formed through the polymerization of amino acids via **peptide bonds**, creating long chains known as polypeptides.
 
• There are **20 standard amino acids** commonly found in proteins, which include essential and non-essential amino acids.
 
• **Essential amino acids** cannot be synthesized by the body and must be obtained through diet, whereas non-essential amino acids can be produced internally.
 
• Amino acids play crucial roles in various biological functions, including enzyme activity, cellular structure, and metabolic processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Peptide Bond**: A chemical bond formed between two amino acids when the carboxyl group of one reacts with the amino group of another, releasing a molecule of water.
 
• **Protein Structure Levels**: Proteins have four structural levels—primary (sequence of amino acids), secondary (alpha-helices and beta-sheets), tertiary (three-dimensional structure), and quaternary (arrangement of multiple polypeptides).
 
• **Role of Proteins**: Proteins function as enzymes, hormones, antibodies, transport molecules, and structural components in cells and tissues.
 
• **Metabolic Pathways**: Amino acids are precursors for important biomolecules like neurotransmitters, nucleotides, and nitrogen-containing compounds.
 
• **Protein Synthesis**: The process involves transcription (DNA to mRNA) and translation (mRNA to protein), utilizing ribosomes and tRNA for the assembly of amino acids.

questions.question:
Which of the following options correctly matches column-A and column-B?

 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 **Column-A (Food component)**
 **Column-B (Enzyme involved in digestion)**
 
 

 i. Protein
 a. Amylase
 
 

 ii. Carbohydrates
 b. Lipase
 
 

 iii. Fats
 c. Trypsin
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 1: i-c, ii-a, iii-b**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Proteins** are broken down by the enzyme **Trypsin**, which is produced in the pancreas and acts in the small intestine.
 
• **Carbohydrates** are digested by **Amylase**, an enzyme found in saliva and pancreatic juice.
 
• **Fats** are digested by the enzyme **Lipase**, which is also produced in the pancreas and acts in the small intestine.
 
• Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up the chemical reactions involved in the digestion of food.
 
• The correct matching of Column-A and Column-B is: i) Protein - Trypsin, ii) Carbohydrates - Amylase, iii) Fats - Lipase.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Proteins:** Complex molecules that are broken down into amino acids, which are essential for various body functions.
 
• **Carbohydrates:** Organic compounds that serve as a major energy source for the body, broken down into simple sugars like glucose.
 
• **Fats:** Lipid molecules that are broken down into fatty acids and glycerol, providing a concentrated energy source.
 
• **Amylase:** An enzyme that helps in the breakdown of starches into sugars, found in saliva and pancreatic juice.
 
• **Trypsin:** A protease enzyme that breaks down proteins into smaller peptides, produced by the pancreas.
 
• **Lipase:** An enzyme that catalyzes the breakdown of fats into fatty acids and glycerol, essential for fat digestion and absorption.

questions.question: Insufficient exposure to sunlight causes deficiency of which vitamin?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vitamin D.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vitamin D **is known as the** sunshine vitamin** because it is produced by the body when the skin is exposed to sunlight.
 
• Insufficient exposure to sunlight can cause a **deficienc****y** of this vitamin.
 
• Vitamin D is important for the absorption of** calcium and phosphorus**, which are essential for **strong bones and teeth.**
 
• A deficiency of **vitamin D** can lead to bone diseases such as rickets in **children and osteomalacia** in adults.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vitamin E and K** are** fat-soluble vitamins **that have different functions in the body.
 
• Vitamin E is an **antioxidant** that protects cells from damage, while** vitamin K **is important for **blood clotting.**
 
• **Vitamin A **is important for **vision, immune function**, and **skin health.**
 
• It is found in animal products such as** liver and dairy,** as well as in plant foods such as** carrots and spinach.**
 
• **Vitamin C** is an antioxidant that is important for **immune function, skin health, and wound healing.**
 
• It is found in** citrus fruits, berries, and leafy greens.**

questions.question: Which among the following Vitamins plays an essential role in vision?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vitamin A:-**

 
 
• It​ plays an essential role in** vision **as it helps to maintain a **healthy retina.**
 
• It also helps in the production of a protein called** rhodopsin,** which enables the** retina to absorb light.**
 
• **Vitamin A** deficiency can lead to **night blindness **and other eye problems. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vitamin C **is commonly found in fruits such as** oranges, strawberries, and kiwis, and vegetables** such as broccoli, bell peppers, and tomatoes.
 
• **Vitamin B1** is commonly found in foods such as** whole grains, meat, fish, and beans.**
 
• **Vitamin D** is commonly found in foods such as **fatty fish, egg yolks, and fortified dairy products,** and can also be synthesized by the body through exposure to sunlight.

questions.question:
Match the columns.

 Column-A(Nutrients) Column-B(Source)

i. Protein rich diet a. Glucose and other sugars

ii. Fat rich diet b. Citrus fruits

iii. Carbohydrate rich diet c. Egg white and red meat
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**i-c, ii-d, iii-a, iv-b**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Protein-rich diet** is primarily derived from **sources such as egg white and red meat**. Proteins are essential for building and repairing body tissues, enzymes, and hormones.
 
• **Fat-rich diet** is commonly found in **butter and cheese**. Fats provide a concentrated source of energy and are crucial for the absorption of fat-soluble vitamins.
 
• **Carbohydrate-rich diet** is abundant in **glucose and other sugars**. Carbohydrates serve as the body's primary energy source and are readily metabolized.
 
• **Vitamin C-rich diet** can be obtained from **citrus fruits** such as oranges and lemons. Vitamin C is vital for boosting immunity, collagen synthesis, and antioxidant protection.
 
• Matching the columns helps in understanding the correlation between **nutrients and their dietary sources**, which is crucial for nutritional science and health-related exams.
 
• Understanding the dietary sources of nutrients aids individuals in maintaining a balanced diet and preventing deficiencies.
 
• These nutrients play a significant role in various **physiological and biochemical functions** essential for overall health and well-being.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Protein-rich diet (Incorrect Match in Other Options)**__

 __
 
• **Proteins** are composed of amino acids, which are categorized as essential and non-essential.
 
• Sources of protein include **animal-based foods** like meat, fish, poultry, and dairy products, and **plant-based foods** like legumes, nuts, and seeds.
 
• Protein deficiency can lead to **muscle loss, weakened immunity**, and delayed wound healing.
 
 
 
• **Fat-rich diet (Incorrect Match in Other Options)**__
 __
 
• **Fats** are classified into saturated, unsaturated, and trans fats. Unsaturated fats are considered healthier.
 
• Common sources include **nuts, seeds, fatty fish, and oils** such as olive oil and sunflower oil.
 
• Excessive consumption of fats, especially saturated and trans fats, can lead to **obesity and cardiovascular diseases**.
 
 
 
• **Carbohydrate-rich diet (Incorrect Match in Other Options)**__
 __
 
• **Carbohydrates** are divided into simple and complex carbs. Complex carbs like whole grains are healthier as they provide sustained energy.
 
• Sources include **rice, bread, pasta, fruits, and vegetables.**
 
• Carbohydrates are essential for **brain function** and physical activity.
 
 
 
• **Vitamin C-rich diet (Incorrect Match in Other Options)**__
 
 
• **Vitamin C** is water-soluble and must be consumed regularly as it is not stored in the body.
 
• Besides citrus fruits, other sources include **berries, kiwi, guava, and leafy greens**.
 
• Vitamin C deficiency can lead to **scurvy**, characterized by bleeding gums and weakened immunity.

questions.question: Which of the following vitamins helps to keep our skin and eyes healthy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vitamin A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vitamin A:**
 
• This vitamin is crucial for maintaining the health of both your skin and eyes.
 
• It is a fat-soluble vitamin that plays an essential role in ensuring normal vision.
 
• It produces pigments in the retina of the eye and promotes good vision, especially in low light.
 
• It also helps the heart, lungs, kidneys, and other organs function properly.
 
• Moreover, it is involved in the regulation of the immune system.
 
• For the skin, vitamin A helps to speed up healing, prevent breakouts, and support the skin's immune system, promoting natural moisturising.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
 

 Vitamin
 Role in Skin Health
 Role in Eye Health
 
 

 Vitamin C
 As an antioxidant, helps to protect the skin from damaging free radicals caused by UV exposure. Aids in the skin's natural regeneration process and helps prevent dry skin.
 Supports the health of blood vessels in the eye and might decrease the risk of cataracts.
 
 

 Vitamin D
 May contribute to skin health by managing the growth of cells and reducing inflammation.
 Some research points to vitamin D deficiency being associated with an increased risk of age-related macular degeneration, but its role in eye health is less established.
 
 

 
 Vitamin B (B3, B5, B7, B2, B6, B9, B12)

 

 

 

 
 
 B3 and B5 improve skin hydration, reduce redness and inflammation, and boost skin elasticity. B7 promotes healthy hair, skin, and nails. 
 B2 helps prevent cataracts. A combination of B6, B9, and B12 might reduce the risk of age-related macular degeneration.

questions.question: Vitamin D is synthesised using sunshine, by the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**skin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The skin synthesizes Vitamin D when exposed to ultraviolet B (UVB) radiation from sunlight.
 
• Vitamin D synthesis occurs when 7-dehydrocholesterol in the skin absorbs UVB light, converting it into pre-vitamin D3, which is then transformed into active Vitamin D (calcitriol) in the liver and kidneys.
 
• Approximately 10–30 minutes of sun exposure, a few times a week, is sufficient for most people to produce adequate Vitamin D levels, depending on skin type and geographical location.
 
• The process is influenced by factors such as time of day, season, latitude, skin pigmentation, and sunscreen usage.
 
• Vitamin D plays a crucial role in calcium absorption, bone health, immune function, and overall well-being.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **7-dehydrocholesterol:** A precursor molecule found in the skin that absorbs UVB radiation to initiate Vitamin D synthesis.
 
• **Calcitriol (Active Vitamin D):** The biologically active form of Vitamin D, which is essential for maintaining calcium and phosphate homeostasis in the body.
 
• **Deficiency Risks:** Lack of sufficient sunlight exposure or dietary intake can lead to Vitamin D deficiency, causing rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults.
 
• **Dietary Sources:** While sunlight is the primary source, Vitamin D can also be obtained from foods like fatty fish, egg yolks, fortified dairy products, and supplements.
 
• **UVB Radiation:** A type of ultraviolet light with wavelengths between 280–315 nm, critical for Vitamin D production but also associated with the risk of skin damage and cancer if overexposed.

questions.question: Excessive bleeding from wounds may happen due to lack of ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vitamin K**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Vitamin K** is an essential nutrient required for blood clotting (coagulation) and preventing excessive bleeding from wounds.
 
• It helps in the synthesis of proteins such as **prothrombin**, which are crucial for the blood clotting process.
 
• A deficiency in Vitamin K can result in **impaired clotting**, leading to prolonged bleeding and easy bruising.
 
• Newborns are particularly at risk of Vitamin K deficiency, which is why they are often given Vitamin K injections at birth to prevent **Vitamin K Deficiency Bleeding (VKDB)**.
 
• Vitamin K is found in green leafy vegetables like spinach, kale, and broccoli, as well as in smaller amounts in dairy products, meat, and eggs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Vitamin K:**

 
 
• **Vitamin K1 (Phylloquinone):** Found primarily in plant-based foods such as green leafy vegetables.
 
• **Vitamin K2 (Menaquinone):** Found in fermented foods and animal products and also produced by gut bacteria.
 
 
 
• **Role in Bone Health:** Vitamin K also plays a role in bone metabolism by helping to regulate calcium levels in the body and supporting bone mineralization.
 
• **Symptoms of Deficiency:** In addition to excessive bleeding, Vitamin K deficiency may cause symptoms like blood in stool or urine, nosebleeds, and heavy menstrual bleeding.
 
• **Vitamin K Antagonists:** Drugs like warfarin act as Vitamin K antagonists and are used to prevent blood clots in conditions such as deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and atrial fibrillation.
 
• **Daily Requirement:** The recommended daily intake of Vitamin K varies by age and gender, with adult males requiring approximately 120 micrograms and adult females requiring about 90 micrograms per day.
